subject.title: fix(signal): preserve durable ingress retry ownership

question: Should this protected Signal reliability change be accepted after confirming that disabling nested dispatch retries preserves durable claim cleanup and shutdown behavior for every Signal ingress path?
rationale: The `maintainer` label requires explicit human handling, and retry ownership crosses durable queue, session initialization, and shutdown lifecycle boundaries that cannot safely be accepted from the supplied patch excerpt alone.

options.title: Confirm the owner boundary and merge
options.body: Review the Signal outer flush lifecycle against the shared dispatch retry contract, then accept the targeted override if it preserves claim abandonment and cancellation.

options.title: Require a narrower lifecycle adjustment
options.body: Keep nested retry behavior only where the shared dispatcher owns the durable claim lifecycle, and make Signal’s ownership boundary explicit in focused coverage.

options.title: Pause for broader retry-contract design
options.body: Defer this PR if the correct retry owner cannot be established without changing shared channel-inbound contracts.

recommendation.title: Confirm the owner boundary and merge
recommendation.body: Review the Signal outer flush lifecycle against the shared dispatch retry contract, then accept the targeted override if it preserves claim abandonment and cancellation.

likelyOwner.reason: The supplied commit history shows steipete authored the current retry-owner and test-harness changes.
